title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week saw a mix of triumphs and setbacks across the space sector, with Skyroot Aerospace successfully reaching orbit while NASA pulled the plug on its lunar lander mission. Meanwhile, funding for space resilience is on the rise, and the competition for orbital dominance continues to heat up.

themes.title: Skyroot's Successful Launch
themes.body: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 launch marks a notable achievement for India's private space sector, potentially setting the stage for more commercial endeavors. This success could inspire further investment and innovation in a region that’s been historically overshadowed by larger players.

themes.title: NASA's Lunar Setback
themes.body: The termination of the Draper lunar lander mission underscores the challenges NASA faces in its ambitious lunar objectives. This decision raises questions about the agency's strategy and its ability to meet future exploration timelines.

themes.title: Funding for Space Resilience
themes.body: The $1.4 billion boost to the space resilience line in the FY27 budget reflects a growing recognition of the need for robust capabilities in an increasingly contested space environment. This funding could catalyze advancements in technologies aimed at protecting U.S. interests in orbit.

themes.title: SpaceX's Ongoing Challenges
themes.body: SpaceX's aborted Starship Flight 13 launch attempt highlights the complexities of scaling operations amidst a rapidly expanding portfolio. As the company grapples with logistical constraints, its competitors may see an opportunity to capitalize on any delays.
